outcome: dystocia during the active first stage of labor (AFSOL)
cohort: 656 laboring women at Debre Markos Comprehensive Specialized Hospital in Northwest Ethiopia were enrolled using systematic random sampling.
finding: The incidence of dystocia during the active first stage of labor was 35.3%, with ANC follow-up, linseed consumption, and ambulation being protective factors, while caffeine intake, labor induction, early admission, and poor provider support increased the risk.
